title: Unified trace format translator and sink negotiator
creator: Sara Lin
description: Build a lightweight translator/negotiator service that sits at the front of the tracing ingest path and normalizes trace payloads and sink routing. The translator will accept multiple incoming encodings (OTLP/gRPC protobuf, OTLP/HTTP, Jaeger Thrift/HTTP) and perform: 1) format normalization into a canonical internal model; 2) capability negotiation with downstream sinks (Tempo, Jaeger, long-term archive) to decide best-fit encoding; 3) field mapping (span tags, resource attributes, sampling meta) and schema-version translation; 4) small, safe mutations needed for compatibility (traceid/spanid padding, legacy-tag renames); and 5) robust failure and degrade paths (retry, buffer, fallback to best-effort sink and metrics/events to alerting). The goal is to reduce per-tenant ingest errors, remove manual per-sink adapters in customers' pipelines, and provide a single place for format compatibility logic and rollout control.
acceptance_criteria: Translator accepts OTLP/gRPC, OTLP/HTTP (protobuf), and Jaeger/Thrift payloads and converts them to canonical model without losing key span attributes
Negotiation protocol: translator queries sink capabilities (supported encodings, max-batch-size, required tags) and selects the optimal sink/encoding for each tenant or route

On upstream schema mismatch the translator performs supported safe transforms (traceid normalization, timestamp rounding if required, tag renames) and emits a structured warning metric and span annotation
End-to-end tests demonstrate <1% increase in p50/p95 ingestion latency for steady load; translator scales horizontally and keeps 99.9% of requests successful under normal traffic profiles
Failure modes: when a downstream sink rejects a batch, translator retries with backoff and if persistent failure occurs, it falls back to alternate sink and emits incident-quality alerting
Telemetry: translator exports internal metrics (ingest_rate, parse_errors, transform_count, sink_negotiation_latency, fallback_rate) and structured logs with tenant/context IDs
Rollout plan validated in canary with 2 tenants and staged expansion to 25% traffic before full rollout
Documentation: README, operational runbook, and compatibility matrix published in Confluence and linked from Console troubleshooting pages
updates: 2026-02-12: Initial spike completed; prototype can parse OTLP protobuf and Jaeger thrift locally. Decided on canonical model based on OpenTelemetry semantic conventions + a small Redwood extension bag for legacy tags.

2026-02-18: Design review with infra and console teams. Agreed to expose negotiation via a light-weight capability handshake: sinks publish a CapabilitySet over the control-plane API; translator caches capabilities for 30s.
2026-02-24: Chose to implement translator as sidecar-able microservice behind the existing trace ingress LB. This keeps path-compatible with current tenants and simplifies gradual traffic migration.
2026-02-28: Security reviewed header passthrough: tenant auth headers are forwarded but sanitized; K8s PSP and mTLS between translator and sinks required per security checklist.
2026-03-03: Implemented tag-rename mapping rules and traceid padding logic. Added counter metrics for each transform rule to discover prevalence of legacy tags.

2026-03-05: Opened PR #7843 (github.com/redwood-inference/observability/PRs/7843) with parsing and canonical model. Integration tests failing on a corner-case timestamp format from Jaeger agent; assigned to eng oncall.
Planned: add deterministic per-tenant routing policy, feature-flagged canary with two internal services, and create dashboard for transform/fallback rates before 25% rollout.
notes: Trade-offs considered: doing translation in the control plane would centralize logic but add latency; chosen approach keeps translation near ingest for lower avg latency and simpler backpressure behavior.

Edge-case: some legacy Jaeger agents send 64-bit traceids. We will normalize by left-padding with zeros and mark those spans with a 'legacy_traceid' attribute so downstream evals can filter them if needed.
Operational concern: capability cache expiry needs tuning to avoid excessive control-plane calls; start with 30s and revisit with perf metrics.
QA: create a corpus of real-world failing spans from past incidents to verify transforms do not degrade sampling fairness or break trace joins in Tempo.
